name: first-snapshot-every-kind
about: A first snapshot (loaded) carrying a named thinking block and unnamed text and tool blocks; the plane's block-row for the named one right after it; chunks of text, a named block's late chunk ignored, a tool call's input; block-rows; a step-end dropping the one block no block-row named; each row landing settles its block.

steps.note: the plane's block-row for a block the snapshot carried named
a chunk for a named block: ignored, its row holds the block whole
the block no block-row named goes; the named ones wait for their rows

about_fixture: DX4's streaming layer, the desk open-fast spec's parity fixture (docs/doperpowers/specs/2026-10-20-desk-open-fast-design.md, section 9), written by sminos/tests/dx4-stream.gen.py: every expected drawing by hand. Each sequence is one session view's messages in order; a step's `message` is a DX4 envelope, or "resubscribe" (the subscription is over and a new one starts: `n` from 0, and its first snapshot is resumed over what is drawn, not loaded). `drawn` is the streaming layer's blocks after the message: agentId ("main" for null) to that agent's blocks in drawing order, an agent with none left out. The store's side, for a replay of the layer alone: `settle` lists the rows whose landing settles blocks after the message, in order (a held row a drawn block awaits; another loop's block-row on a main view); a resumed snapshot's step gives `landing` (the newest row the snapshot brought, null for none) and `lands` (the named rows `lands` answers true for). A sequence's `errors` are the reference consumer's error kinds, in order (gap, dup, watermark, differs, vanished, after-end, marks); `inventory`, where present, is the transcript on disk and the DX5 events the session emitted, and what checking the consumer against them names: holes (rows never delivered), partial (a block drawn while its row was held), vanished (a block gone before its row landed), dups (a row delivered twice, a block drawn again after it settled), undrawn (a block whose request this view followed, never drawn before its row arrived live), residual (the same for a request that had ended before the view followed it: the snapshot between a step's end and its rows' flush, an accepted hole).

name: reconnect-empty-history-carries-the-named-block
about: A2 and A8: a block is named, the subscription is lost, and the fresh snapshot — its history empty, the row not yet on disk — carries the block with its uuid. The block stays drawn with the snapshot's text until its row lands, then goes once. (Today's web dropped it here: no row would land, no newer row came.)

steps.note: the subscription is over; a new one starts and resumes the drawing
resumed: the snapshot carries the named block, so it is drawn from it
the plane's block-row for the carried named block: idempotent

name: reconnect-snapshot-no-longer-carries-the-block
about: The fresh snapshot no longer streams the blocks the old subscription drew: their rows were written in the gap and the snapshot brings them. The named block waits for its own row (it lands: the snapshot merged into the held rows), the unnamed one for the newest row the snapshot brought; both are held, so both settle at once.

steps.note: the subscription is over; a new one starts and resumes the drawing
resumed: merged (its oldest row is held); block 0 settles by its row, block 1 by the landing

name: reconnect-older-snapshot-changes-nothing
about: A fresh snapshot older than what was drawn (its watermark below the drawn one: a producer that went back) changes nothing of that request; the live chunks the drawing holds are dropped at the drawn watermark, the later ones appended.

steps.note: the subscription is over; a new one starts and resumes the drawing
resumed: its watermark 3 is below the drawn 5
at or below the drawn watermark: dropped

name: main-view-carries-a-subagents-named-block
about: A main view carries every agent's streaming. A subagent's block the snapshot carries named is drawn until the plane's block-row for it, which settles it at once (its row comes on the agent's own subscription, never here); the main loop's block waits for its row.

steps.note: another loop's block-row: settled at once

name: planted-vanished-and-a-hole
about: Planted: the fresh snapshot after a disruption carries neither the named block nor its row (what the plane's open gate existed to prevent), and the row is never delivered. The block vanishes before its row landed; the row is a hole.

steps.note: the subscription is over; a new one starts and resumes the drawing
planted: no block, no row; the held rows are replaced

name: planted-partial-and-drawn-twice
about: Planted: a block's row lands before its block-row (the block is drawn beside its row: partial), then a fresh snapshot replaces the held rows and carries the settled block named again (drawn twice).

steps.note: planted: the row before its block-row; the unnamed block stays drawn beside it
the subscription is over; a new one starts and resumes the drawing

name: reconnect-fresh-text-and-the-old-name
about: Blocks the fresh snapshot carries unnamed are drawn with its text: one still streaming takes the snapshot's newer text and goes on; one the old subscription had named keeps that name, so its row settles it.

steps.note: the subscription is over; a new one starts and resumes the drawing
resumed: block 0 the snapshot's text; block 1 carried unnamed keeps the old name

name: planted-undrawn-and-the-residual-hole
about: Planted: the first snapshot follows a request still streaming (block 1) but carries neither its named block 0 nor that block's row, which arrives live after its block-row: the block was never drawn (the first open's twin of the carried-block loss). Beside it, the row of a request whose step had ended before the snapshot arrives live too, its block never drawn and its request never followed: the snapshot fell between that step's end and its rows' flush, the hole the design accepts (residual).

steps.note: planted: block 0 of the request, named, is missing; so is its row
the residual: an ended step's row, after a snapshot that could carry neither
names a block that is not drawn

name: truncated-blocks-settle
about: Blocks whose catch-up copy the producer cut to its last characters (`truncated`, the spec's section 7): a text block and a tool call whose kept input is the tail of its JSON, not JSON whole. Each is drawn with the tail it carries and settles cleanly by its row, whose text, or whose input as serialized, ends with that tail.
